vulnerability_analysis: The contract is a reflection token with fee-on-transfer mechanics. The vulnerability 'Transfer Revert Propagation' likely exists in the marketing fee distribution. The swapAndSendMarketing() function uses payable(marketingWallet).sendValue(newBalance) which returns a boolean but doesn't check it. If sendValue() fails (returns false), the transaction continues without reverting. This means if marketingWallet is a contract that reverts on receive, the ETH from marketing fees remains stuck in the contract instead of being sent out. An attacker could potentially extract this stuck ETH.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the owner to change marketing wallet to an attack contract that reverts on receive. 2. Generate contract token balance through trading (fees accumulate in contract). 3. Trigger the swap mechanism by selling tokens, which will call swapAndSendMarketing(). 4. The sendValue() will fail but transaction continues, leaving ETH in contract. 5. Extract the stuck ETH through other means (like price manipulation or owner functions).
step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy an attack contract that reverts in its receive() function. 2. Use vm.prank to impersonate the contract owner. 3. Call changeMarketingWallet() to set marketing wallet to attack contract. 4. Enable trading if not already enabled. 5. Buy tokens to generate fee accumulation in contract. 6. Sell tokens to trigger swap mechanism. 7. The swapAndSendMarketing will fail but continue, leaving ETH in contract. 8. Find way to extract ETH (possibly through buy/sell price differences due to stuck ETH).
